question.text: Fund TCR is a Category III AIF running a '130/30' long-short strategy with INR 500 crore investable corpus. What is the fund's net market exposure and gross exposure respectively?

answer.text: Net 100%, Gross 160% (INR 500 cr net, INR 800 cr gross)
Net 130%, Gross 130% (INR 650 cr net, INR 650 cr gross)
Net 100%, Gross 130% (INR 500 cr net, INR 650 cr gross)
Net 160%, Gross 100% (INR 800 cr net, INR 500 cr gross)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.2.1.2 (Long-Short Equity strategy), a 130/30 fund takes 130% long and 30% short as a percentage of investable funds. Net exposure = 130 - 30 = 100% (INR 500 cr). Gross exposure = 130 + 30 = 160% (INR 800 cr). The fund is fully invested long-equivalent but with an additional sleeve from the short leg. The Trap: Option B confuses net with absolute leverage. Option C under-sizes the gross by ignoring the short leg's gross contribution. Option D inverts the formula entirely. Note: The 2x NAV leverage cap for Category III AIFs (per the AIF leverage page) constrains the gross exposure that a Cat III fund can run.
